title: Surjective on cohomology of the principal-open Cech augmentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, $V=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$ and $D_S=D(\prod_{j\in S}f_j)$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary unbounded K-injective cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $K,T$ be complexes of $A$-modules, with degreewise $A$-linear isomorphisms $\sigma_n:K^n\cong\Gamma(V,J^n)$ and $\tau_n:T^n\cong\prod_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)}\Gamma(D_S,J^{n+1-|S|})$. Assume $\sigma$ identifies the differential of $K$ with the sectionwise differential of $J$, and $\tau$ identifies the differential of $T$ with the signed total formula: at $S$ its vertical term is $(-1)^{|S|-1}d_J$ and its horizontal term is the sum over $j\in S$ of restriction from $D_{S\setminus\{j\}}$, multiplied by $(-1)^{|\{i\in S:i<j\}|}$, with empty deletions zero. All coefficient degrees are transported by their displayed integer equalities. Let $\alpha:K\to T$ be a chain map which under these coordinates is restriction from $V$ on singleton coordinates and zero on all larger subsets. The open inclusion inequalities and degree equalities in the Lean signature specify only the transports in these formulas. Then $H^n(\alpha)$ is surjective for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Restrict J to V via overFunctor followed by overEquiv V. Open restriction preserves K-injectivity, and the module equivalence preserves it. The inverse images of the principal opens cover V: preimage commutes with iSup and the preimage of V by its inclusion is top.

Apply the existing finite-cover K-injective alternating Cech augmentation quasi-isomorphism theorem on the scheme V.toScheme to the restricted complex. No new row-exactness or staircase argument is needed.

The subset comparison gives an arrow isomorphism after forgetting the two scalar actions. Exact module forgetful functors preserve and reflect quasi-isomorphisms. Transfer the forgotten tuple quasi-isomorphism across the arrow isomorphism, reflect it to alpha in A-modules, and infer that every homology map is an isomorphism and hence an epimorphism.
